hook: Joseph Weizenbaum was born on January 8, 1923, in Berlin, Germany, and fled with his family to the United States in the 1930s as the Nazi regime tightened its persecution of Jews. He studied mathematics at Wayne University in Detroit, worked on early digital computers there, and later helped design the ERMA banking computer system at General Electric in the 1950s. In 1963 he joined the faculty of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and in 1966 he published ELIZA, a program that used simple pattern matching to imitate a psychotherapist's responses, in a paper for Communications of the ACM. Weizenbaum was troubled that people, including his own secretary, treated ELIZA's replies as though they carried real understanding, and the experience turned him into one of computing's most prominent internal critics. In his 1976 book Computer Power and Human Reason he argued that some human judgments should never be delegated to a machine, a position he held until his death on March 5, 2008, in Berlin.

quick_facts: Born January 8, 1923, in Berlin, Germany, and died March 5, 2008, in Berlin.
Fled Nazi Germany with his family and settled in the United States in the 1930s.
Studied mathematics at Wayne University in Detroit and later helped design the ERMA banking computer at General Electric.
Published the ELIZA paper in Communications of the ACM in January 1966.
Joined the MIT faculty in 1963 and was later awarded tenure in the Department of Electrical Engineering.
Became a leading critic of artificial intelligence research after observing how people related to ELIZA.

achievements.title: ELIZA (1966)
achievements.impact: Showed that a program with no real understanding of language could still convince people it understood them, launching decades of research and debate over natural language processing and human anthropomorphism of machines.

achievements.title: Computer Power and Human Reason (1976)
achievements.impact: Argued publicly that certain human decisions should not be turned over to computers, shaping early debate on the ethics and limits of artificial intelligence.

achievements.title: ERMA banking system contributions
achievements.impact: Helped build one of the first computer systems used for large-scale commercial data processing, extending digital computing beyond research labs.
